title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation, Known Issues & QBR Playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Purpose:
This playbook consolidates the standard process used by Redwood's Customer Success and Support teams for enterprise onboarding. It covers the integration checklist, escalation paths, common known issues with workarounds, and the health check / QBR (Quarterly Business Review) materials and cadence. The document is intended for CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, and their cross-functional partners (SRE, Product, Eng).

Scope:
- Applies to enterprise customers (Dedicated & Private deployments, committed capacity) during evaluation, onboarding, and the first 90 days post-go-live.
- Includes steps for API/integration validation, data residency checks, SLA handoff, and QBR cadence setup.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs) / Integration Engineers
- Support Engineers and Tier 2 on-call
- Account Executives (for contract-specific items)

Quick summary / owner map:
- CSM: overall onboarding project owner, QBRs, customer-facing comms
- SE: integration plan, API verification, test plan sign-off
- Support Engineer (Tier 2): post-go-live incident triage and escalation
- Eng/SRE: capacity and performance escalations (see escalation matrix)

Onboarding phases (high level):
1) Discovery (2-5 business days)
   - Outputs: requirements doc, data residency & compliance checklist, reference architecture sign-off
   - Owner: CSM + SE

2) Integration & Validation (1-3 weeks typical)
   - Tasks:
     - Provide API keys and example requests (SE)
     - Customer implements SDK / REST calls for generation, chat, and embeddings
     - Integration checklist: auth, region routing, model pinning, rate-limits, webhook setup for streaming
     - Run integration smoke tests (see Test Plan table below)
   - Success criteria (required to progress): end-to-end sample generation, embedding upsert+query, < 100ms p50 latency for test harness (hosted), and passing the security checklist

3) Pre-Go-live Validation (1 week)
   - Load testing with customer traffic profile (SE + Eng SRE)
   - Validate caching and batching settings, KV-cache warmup, and cost estimates from Redwood Optimize
   - Confirm rollback & canary policies are documented

4) Go-live & 0-30 days support (30 days)
   - Monitor SLOs (see SLO section), attend daily standup with customer for first 3 days, transition to weekly health checks after day 7

5) Handover to NBD (30-90 days)
   - Transition to regular QBR cadence and support SLAs, finalize playbook for runbook additions

Integration checklist (table view - copy into Confluence table):
- Customer account created and scoped (region, VPC)
- API keys issued; key rotation policy documented
- Model catalog & versions pinned for first rollout
- Rate limit & quota configuration confirmed
- Webhooks/Streaming endpoint validated (TLS, IP allowlist)
- Embeddings index & similarity test queries executed
- Monitoring dashboards provisioned (latency/cost/throughput)
- Security/compliance controls validated (KMS, audit logs, data residency)
content_addendum:
Test Plan (examples):
1) Functional smoke tests (post-integration):
   - POST /v1/generate with a 64-token prompt -> expect coherent output and 200 response
   - POST /v1/embeddings -> upsert 100 vectors, run nearest-neighbor query -> expected recall >= 0.75 on curated dataset
2) Performance validation:
   - 95th percentile token latency under target (hosted: p95 <= 350ms for 256-token responses; dedicated depends on plan)
   - Throughput validation: maintain target RPS for 30-minute sustained window

Escalation playbook (step-by-step):
Severity levels and SLAs:
- Sev1 (Service Down / Data loss) – initial response: 15 minutes, target mitigation: 4 hours
- Sev2 (High-impact degradation) – initial response: 30 minutes, target mitigation: 24 hours
- Sev3 (Functional impact to some users) – initial response: 4 business hours, target mitigation: 3 business days
- Sev4 (Low-impact / Enhancement request) – initial response: 2 business days, target mitigation: per roadmap

Escalation matrix (who to contact):
- Customer-facing Support (Tier 1): first triage, create ticket in JIRA/Support portal, gather logs, request consent for additional debug traces
- Support Engineer (Tier 2): assigned by on-call rotation; responsible for deeper troubleshooting and reproducing issue
- Eng-SRE on-call: invoked for capacity, performance, networking (contact via PagerDuty, escalation channel: #sre-oncall)
- Runtime / Model Engineering: engaged by Support/Tier2 for kernel/kernel-selection or model-specific regressions
- Customer Success Director: engaged when contract SLA or executive visibility required

Escalation steps (numbered procedure):
1) Tier 1 validates customer identity and gathers the required triage checklist (API request IDs, timestamps, region, model ID, payload sample)
2) If reproducible and service-impacting, promote to Tier 2 and attach runbook run results
3) Tier 2 attempts mitigation: restart worker pool, modify batching window, or route traffic to fallback model variant
4) If mitigation requires infra changes or capacity, page Eng-SRE and include recent perf profiles and the repro harness
5) Communicate status every 60 minutes for Sev1 until mitigation achieved; use templated customer status updates

Contact & escalation table (copy for internal use):
- Support portal: support.redwood.ai -> creates ticket with ID
- PagerDuty: SRE on-call (alias: redwood-sre-oncall)
- Slack channels: #support-urgent, #sre-oncall, #runtime-dev

Known issues and workarounds (concise table rows):
- Symptom: Intermittent 503s during burst traffic
  - Likely cause: short-term worker pool exhaustion or load balancer timeout
  - Workaround: enable burst capacity (Dedicated customers), temporarily reduce batch size to lower memory per-request, route to fallback model variant
- Symptom: Embedding similarity score drop after model upgrade
  - Likely cause: model semantics shift post-upgrade
  - Workaround: pin previous model for critical endpoints, re-run embedding index rebuild on new model and update threshold calibration
- Symptom: Slow initial token generation for long-context requests
  - Likely cause: KV cache cold start or suboptimal kernel for sequence length
  - Workaround: warm KV cache using representative prompts prior to go-live window; request runtime tune (kernel hint) from runtime team
- Symptom: Audit log gaps for private deployments
  - Likely cause: misconfigured forwarding to customer SIEM or KMS permission issues
  - Workaround: verify forwarding configuration, confirm KMS grants, escalate to Private Deployments team if logs still missing

Support process & ticket lifecycle:
- Ticket creation: Customer or SE opens ticket via support portal or email; auto-ack with ticket ID within 5 minutes
- Triage: Tier 1 validates and assigns severity within 30 minutes of ticket creation
- Investigation: Tier 2 reproduces in staging or dedicated repro harness; attach findings to ticket
- Remediation: Live mitigation steps (router fallback, config change) are implemented; follow-up postmortem for Sev1/Sev2
- Closure: Customer confirmation of fix required for closure; link to postmortem if applicable

SLOs and monitoring (operational metrics to surface in QBR):
- Uptime SLO: 99.9% monthly for Hosted APIs (enterprise SLAs vary by contract)
- Request success rate: target >= 99.5% (exclude planned maintenance windows)
- Latency targets (hosted): p50 <= 75ms, p95 <= 350ms for 256-token generation baseline
- Embedding indexing cadence: indexes should complete within agreed window (typical SLA: <= 24 hours for up to 1M vectors)
- Error budget policy: 3x missed SLOs in a quarter triggers reliability review and remediation plan

Health checks & QBR materials (cadence and templates):
- 7-day health check (first week after go-live): daily sync for first 3 days, then 2x weekly for remainder of week
- 30-day health check: weekly cadence; focus on usage patterns, cost anomalies, and initial model quality regressions
- QBR (quarterly): CSM-led with SE and Account Exec; agenda to include:
  1) Executive summary (uptime, major incidents, cost delta vs forecast)
  2) Usage trends by product area (generation vs embeddings usage)
  3) Model performance and quality regressions (prompt-based evals and key prompts)
  4) Optimization opportunities (caching, quantization suggestions from Redwood Optimize)
  5) Action items and ownership (with dates)

QBR deliverables (checklist):
- Dashboard snapshot (latency, success rate, cost per 1K tokens)
- Incident review summary (if any Sev1/2 in quarter)
- Prompt-based quality report (selected prompts + eval metrics)
- Optimization roadmap (recommended config changes and expected unit-cost impact)

Templates (copy/paste into Confluence):
- Customer status update template (for Sev1):
  "We are actively investigating an issue impacting X customers. Current status: mitigation in progress. Next update in 60 minutes. Incident ID: {{ticket_id}}. Point of contact: {{csm_name}}."
